evals.name: beginner-no-dbt
evals.setup: Copy the fixture to a temp dir. Run with a PATH that has no dbt on it and no .venv in the project. Helper installed.
evals.prompt:
/erd-studio-setup

hi! total beginner here. my team lead said to install this ERD Studio thing and point it at our dbt repo so I can see how the tables connect. I don't think I even have dbt installed on this laptop, is that a problem?
evals.expected_output: A warm, plain-English walkthrough that explains dbt is optional, asks one question about where dbt might be installed, then carries on from the project files alone. It proposes one default domain from the schema.yml models (dim_customer, dim_product, fct_orders, fct_shipments), writes logical-models yml files and a domain JSON whose relationships are copied from the inventory, runs the diff and reports an honest result.
expectations: Explains that dbt is optional for ERD Studio before or alongside any install instructions
Asks the user to paste the output of `which dbt` / `where dbt` from their usual environment before giving install steps
Does not run any dbt install command without the user agreeing
Defines 'domain' and 'layer' in plain language before asking the user to choose
Proposes one concrete default domain the user can accept with 'yes'
Asks at most one question per message
Writes a domain JSON with schemaVersion 5 whose logical.relationships match the inventory relationships exactly
Does not paste raw JSON output from the helper at the user
Runs `erd-studio diff` after writing the files and reports the result using the diff counts

evals.name: venv-dbt-core
evals.setup: Copy the fixture to a temp dir and delete its .erd-studio/ folder. Create .venv/bin/dbt as a stub script: `--version` prints a dbt Core 1.9.4 block (Core: / - installed: 1.9.4 / Plugins: / - duckdb: 1.9.1); `parse` touches target/manifest.json and exits 0; `docs generate` exits 0. Put a minimal ~/.dbt/profiles.yml with profile 'test' in a temp HOME.
evals.prompt:
/erd-studio-setup orders

we use dbt core, it's in a .venv in the repo. can you get the orders stuff into an ERD for me?
evals.expected_output: Recognises dbt Core 1.x in .venv, explains manifest vs catalog, runs `.venv/bin/dbt parse` by path (no activation), uses 'orders' from $ARGUMENTS without asking for a business area, writes logical models for the order-related models and a domain, runs the diff, fixes any drift on session-created models automatically, and finishes with a success line based on the diff counts.
expectations: Reports that dbt Core 1.x was found in .venv
Runs dbt through the venv path (e.g. `.venv/bin/dbt parse`) rather than `source .venv/bin/activate && dbt ...`
Narrates each command in one sentence before running it
Does not ask which business area to model, because 'orders' was given as an argument
Invokes the /erd-studio skill before writing any .erd-studio file
Warns in advance about the one-time safety check that pauses the first .erd-studio write
Never runs `dbt run`, `dbt build`, `dbt seed` or `dbt snapshot`
The final `erd-studio diff` for the new domain exits 0 (clean)
Shows the numbered 1-6 progress checklist at stage boundaries

Identifies the installation as dbt Fusion (2.x) and explains it in plain language

evals.name: cloud-cli
evals.setup: Copy the fixture to a temp dir and delete .erd-studio/ and target/. Put a stub `dbt` on PATH whose `--version` prints `dbt Cloud CLI - 0.40.14 (abc123 2025-01-01)`; any other command prints an authentication error and exits 1. No profiles.yml anywhere.

evals.name: existing-user-with-logical-models
evals.setup: Copy the fixture as-is (it already has .erd-studio/logical-models/*.yml, several domains, and some v4 domain files). Keep target/manifest.json and target/catalog.json. Stub dbt Core on PATH.
evals.prompt: I've been using ERD Studio for a few months and already have a bunch of logical models. Can you reverse-engineer the rest of my dbt models into a new domain and check everything lines up with dbt? Please don't mess with my existing designs.
evals.expected_output: Notices existing logical models and says they will not be changed without asking. Suggests migrating the older-format domains. References existing logical-models yml files by name without rewriting them. When the diff reports drift on pre-existing models, groups it into one plain-English summary and asks once (default: match dbt). Session-created models are fixed automatically.
expectations: States early that existing logical models will not be changed without asking
Mentions that some existing domains use an older format and suggests 'ERD Studio: Migrate to v5'
Does not overwrite any logical-models/*.yml file that existed before the session unless the user agreed
Asks a single grouped question about drift on pre-existing models, recommending 'keep' because the user asked not to change their existing designs (the usual default is 'match dbt')
Never deletes a logical-models/*.yml file
Does not clear or rewrite viewConfig.positions in any existing domain file

evals.name: thin-project-sql-only
evals.setup: Copy the fixture to a temp dir, then delete target/, .erd-studio/, and every models/**/*.yml so only the .sql files remain (dim_project, dim_region, dim_task, fct_sale, fct_task_event). No dbt on PATH.
evals.prompt:
/erd-studio-setup

our dbt project is pretty bare bones honestly, it's just sql files, we never got round to writing the yml docs. will this still work?
evals.expected_output: Explains plainly that dbt does not list these columns anywhere yet. Offers, in order: running the catalog (not possible here - no dbt), drafting columns from each model's final SELECT marked '(draft)' with types to confirm, and opt-in relationship tests. The final report does not claim a full match and says how many models have no column information in dbt.
expectations: Explains in plain language that dbt has no column information for these models yet
Offers drafting columns from the SQL SELECT list, marking them '(draft)'
Lists drafted or guessed column types under a 'types to confirm' heading or list
Asks before adding any relationships tests to dbt yml files (opt-in), and uses `severity: warn` if it adds them
Does not invent relationships in the domain JSON that no dbt relationships test declares
The final summary says how many models have no column information in dbt, rather than claiming everything matches

evals.name: modelling-kimball
evals.setup: Copy the fixture to a temp dir and delete its .erd-studio/ folder. Keep target/manifest.json. Stub dbt Core 1.9 on PATH; minimal profiles.yml with profile 'test'. Helper installed. WebSearch/WebFetch available.
evals.prompt:
/erd-studio-setup orders

We follow Kimball — star schemas, conformed dimensions, and we keep customer history.
evals.expected_output: Uses the Kimball description the user already gave instead of confirming the detected style (its words beat the detection). Narrates a lookup of Kimball's standards (kimballgroup.com or dbt docs) or says it is using ERD Studio's bundled summary, plays back 3-6 concrete rules and asks 'Sound right?'. Saves .erd-studio/modelling-approach.md with the user's words quoted verbatim, the rules, the field mapping, sources and date. Model yml files carry modelRole (valid values only), grain, isNaturalKey/additiveType where they apply and a rationale citing the approach, while columns, types, keys and relationships still match dbt so the diff is clean. After the diff, a conformance review notes that dim_customer does not keep history today and offers keep-in-sync (default) or target design.
expectations: Does not ask the user to confirm a detected style or how the team models data, because the user already described it; plays their description back instead
Names the source used for the rules (a URL such as kimballgroup.com / docs.getdbt.com, or 'ERD Studio's bundled summary')
Plays back between 3 and 6 concrete rule bullets and asks for confirmation with a yes default
Writes .erd-studio/modelling-approach.md containing the user's sentence verbatim in quotes, a rules list, a field-mapping section, sources and a date
Every modelRole written is one of conformed-dim, domain-dim, transaction-fact, periodic-snapshot, accumulating-snapshot, factless-fact, reference, gold-fact, gold-dim
fct_order.yml has a grain and modelRole transaction-fact; dim_customer.yml has modelRole conformed-dim
Does not add, rename or remove any column or relationship because of the approach
The final `erd-studio diff` for the new domain exits 0 (clean)
Runs a conformance review after the clean diff, offering keep-in-sync as the default and describing target design as intentional differences
Does not write scdType: 2 on dim_customer columns unless the dbt model actually keeps history (snapshot or validity columns)
customer_id on dim_customer carries isNaturalKey: true (the source system's key, also the PK); email is not flagged as a natural key
The target-design offer says history, key and grain targets are recorded in the backlog and rationale, not in scdType or the key flags

evals.name: modelling-data-vault

(When the skill states the modelling style it detected and asks 'Sound right?', answer instead: "Data Vault 2.0 — hubs, links and satellites in the raw vault, with Kimball-style information marts on top.")

The user overrides it in their own words; the skill identifies Data Vault 2.0 plus Kimball marts, looks the standard up or uses the bundled summary, and plays back the rules. expectations: Confirms the detected style (medallion silver → gold, Kimball-style dim_/fct_ tables) in one sentence with evidence and a yes default, alone in its message — never an open 'how do you model data?' question
Accepts the user's override in their own words and follows it instead of the detected style
Identifies both Data Vault 2.0 and Kimball information marts in the answer
Explains that hubs/links/satellites have no exact ERD Studio role and says how they would be recorded (closest modelRole plus rationale.roleChoice)
Never writes a modelRole value outside the nine valid values (no 'hub', 'link' or 'satellite')
Saves .erd-studio/modelling-approach.md naming Data Vault 2.0 and the mart style
The final `erd-studio diff` for the new domain exits 0 (clean)

evals.expected_output: Detects Kimball-style marts from the dim_/fct_ names (no layering: only a marts folder) and confirms it with the evidence and a yes default. On 'not sure' it goes with the detected style. With no web tool it says it is using ERD Studio's bundled summary. Plays back the rules, saves the approach file and applies it without creating drift.

Treats 'not sure' as a yes to the detected style, without a second question about it

Plays back the rules and asks 'Sound right?' (or equivalent) with a yes default
Saves .erd-studio/modelling-approach.md recording the detection evidence and that the user was not sure
The step-3 checklist line reads 'Choose a business area and modelling style'
Asks at most one question per message
